searchText: Am i wrong in assuming throughput will be lower post eip1559 because blocks will have to become less than half full in order for base fee to go down. So less than half full blocks - which is the equivalent of a less than full block today - will be more common because the market is waiting for basefee to adjust down if true maybe miners will just increase gas limit a bit to offset this 🙂 who knows Okay We've been discussing about optimizing the block production by removing transactions that are not very profitable to mine Smaller blocks are faster to propagate, so this would mean a huge improvement in the uncle rate <@354681205842771973> last time <@486501030046203915> did the math, it seemed like about 2 gwei in tip compensates for the uncle risk. Is that roughly what you are aiming for? Here's the write up: https://notes.ethereum.org/@barnabe/rk5ue1WF_ Not really It's either to mine 2.03 ETH and risk the block being uncle, either mine 2 ETH with the minimum risk of it getting uncled Assuming that the 2 ETH empty blocks will have 1% uncle rate, and full blocks will have 5%: Mining full blocks avg block reward: (1.75 * 0.05 + 2.03*0.95) = 1.98745 ETH Mining empty blocks avg block reward: (1.75 * 0.01 + 2*0.99) = 1.9975 ETH Mining empty blocks will also help miners to cut their node operating costs. I approximate 2x cost reduction Miners could also mine MEV on those empty blocks Giving miners transaction fees was a fix to this Last time I checked, each ~10m gas adds a ~2% risk of being uncled I would say around 3% This is the rate of empty blocks on Ethereum mainnet Yeah, at 15m gas, so that lines up, right? Ah yes 10m -> 2%, 15m -> 3% The gas limit is 15m Yes So at 3%, full blocks = 2.0216 on avg, and empty = 1.9975 This issue still persists though We can mine really expensive MEV transactions only You can mine MEV on full blocks too? Yes But that will add the risk of being uncled <@!486501030046203915>'s numbers here capture that risk in the gwei price: https://notes.ethereum.org/@barnabe/rk5ue1WF_ I remember when our block with 20 ETH MEV got uncled. It wouldn't been a case if we mined that transaction only Well, another miner could choose to uncle you if they see such a high MEV block 😛 But that aside, yeah, it may be worth having a special edge case for very high MEV blocks I'm not sure exactly where the line is though in terms of it warranting an edge case. 20ETH probably makes sense, 2 ETH maybe not? > 2 ETH maybe not? Also does 2x the block reward 4 ETH instead of 2.03 ETH At the end of the day, miners can stop including transactions that are not profitable to them So users will be forced to pay the same gas fee to the miner as miner tip besides the base fee Which will only make fees on eth higher Assuming all miners have the same threshold, but miners with lower costs basically have an incentive to accept txns from those users because it's 'free money' Yeah But again If there is a transaction that pays 2 ETH, for example Miner will be incentivized to mine a block just with that transaction That would be the most profitable approach Yeah, so I think in that case you basically want the average tip to cover something like 80% of the MEV opportunity costs and if, say, the top 20% results in blocks with just that bundle, then the next block can be 2x as large to accommodate the extra pending txns I'm very skeptical about the next block being 2x as large Gas price oracles usually look at recent 20-50 blocks What does that have to do with block size? If there are X txns which couldn't get in the MEV block, and Y that get sent in the meantime, then why not include X+Y? I'm talking about 2x rewards Assuming that you were talking about rewards here as well I meant 2x as large in terms of txns Ah well So, MEV block has 1 transaction, the bundle But then all the pending txns can be included in the next block Don't think that it would make the next block much more profitable than the previous and by definition, if the tips cover, say, the uncle risk for the 80th percentile MEV blocks, then 96% of the time (1 - .2 * .2) the next block shouldn't have a top 20th-percentile MEV opportunity But again, the reward for including the entire block is 0.03 ETH Which by any means cannot be compared with 2 ETH single transaction Yes, but those are rare, right (Flashbots dashboard loading..) Our avg MEV reward is 0.12 ETH Hahaha Do you have your median or 75th percentile reward? Average gets skewed a lot by the top rewards Also, if there are consecutive blocks where only 1 MEV transaction is included, then the basefee will drop, so an increase in miner tip will help incentivize miners to inlcude the txns without increasing the total txn fee for the user. Ok, dashboard loaded! <:this:808397964833718282> Not true in 100% of cases, but yes, esp. for legacy txns So, as per flashbots, 90% of MEV rewards are <0.1 ETH Where did you find this piece of data? So that means that if the total tips in a block == .1 ETH, then 90% of the time, you'd be better off including all txns basically (+ some flat cost for the uncle risk) https://dashboard.flashbots.net/miners, switch to ETH view, not USD Ty So, if you want to beat 90% of MEV blocks, then a ~6 gwei tip is enough But the 50% mark is closer to .01 ETH so to beat that, you only need a .06 gwei tip and, it's worth noting not all blocks have bundles There are like 60% of blocks with bundles, again as per flashbots so that means if you multiple those numbers by .6, you should still be net better off on average Yeah but keep in mind that MEV is pretty dead atm Yes, those values will need to adjust for sure But it's also worth checking the median vs. mean in this cases because sometimes the extreme outliers make a big difference and it's basically fine for people to not want to compete for inclusion against those txns 6 gwei right now is the gas price cost fyi Correction: ~16 gwei Weird, I see 22 on etherscan, but 6 gwei is probably overkill for most people, because they probably don't care about beating 90% of MEV-blocks, but they care about being in like, the next 2-3 blocks Yeah I was wrong haha Was quite a long time since I've checked the gas price 😄 So if you want to be in the next 2-3 blocks, you prob want to beat the ~50% MEV threshold (esp. because, again, only ~60% of blocks have MEV) > (esp. because, again, only ~60% of blocks have MEV) For now Yep, as that % goes up, then so will the minimum tip! Perhaps Either way, we'll see how it will go But I still do think that there are some ways to mine blocks differently, thus receving more in rewards Yup indeed the note that Tim linked can explicitely include the MEV to give you the priority fee necessary to compensate uncle risk The hope being that super high MEV isn’t so usual so a priority fee that has a bit of margin for comfort (e.g. 2 Gwei) makes it robust to blocks with small MEV Then the tradeoff to deal with higher MEV is having some kind of oracle that can say “wait the next block has a big bundle, you need 5 Gwei priority now” a flowchart for how to pick a gas fee in that situation would be hilariously complex imo but maybe not as bad as it sounds This is true of most software 😛 see: https://magicbell.com/blog/slack-notifications-flowchart It could easily be abstracted away from the user though, assuming that oracle exists i'd expect most pools to have some threshold of MEV that could be included where they bail on including any other transactions. this will be to catch those outliers of very large MEV payouts which only happen occasionally but would suck to lose hello everyone!
